comparisons.peer_topic: Benefit of government incentives on operating income
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, government incentives reduced expenses, benefiting operating income by $588 million, with approximately 85% allocated to COGS and 15% to R&D.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose the impact of government incentives on their 2024 operating income, with both companies attributing a substantial portion of this benefit to cost of sales (COGS). Intel reported that operating-related incentives benefited operating income by $442 million in 2024, with the substantial majority recorded in cost of sales. Similarly, Micron reported that government incentives reduced expenses and benefited operating income by $588 million in 2024, with approximately 85% allocated to COGS and 15% to R&D. While the specific amounts and exact allocation splits differ, both disclosures highlight the materiality of these incentives in reducing expenses and boosting operating income, primarily through the COGS line item.

sentences.text: Operating-related incentives, including those recognized under the CHIPS Act, benefited operating income by $442 million in 2024, the substantial majority of which was recorded in cost of sales ($202 million in 2023 and $104 million in 2022, a majority of which was recorded in cost of sales in both periods).
In 2024, operating income (loss) benefited by $588 million (approximately 85% in COGS and 15% in R&D) from government incentives recognized as a reduction of expense.
